Ava: heads-up — overnight canary on dedicated pool hit a regression after the kernel-switch rollout. large fraction of attention outputs contained NaNs / infs when we picked the new flashx-quant variant with fp8-enabled heuristics. attaching a brief log snippet.

Sam: ugh. how many requests? single route or global? any pattern on seq len / batch?

Ava: mostly one route (chat-io), spike during long-history sessions. ~2.1k requests over 3m. sample log: 
```
[2026-03-17T23:08:12Z] kernel=flashx-quant mode=fp8 batch=32 seq=153 qk_max=1.23e+4 softmax_inf=true output_nan_ratio=0.37
[2026-03-17T23:08:12Z] kv_prefetch=true kv_offset_misaligned=maybe
[2026-03-17T23:08:13Z] fallback->fp16-stable-kernel triggered for 18/32 items
```

Rajat: perf-bot profile (quick): p99 latency +420ms, tokens/s -18%, GPU mem up ~400MB. :chart_with_upwards_trend: linked flame: https://perf.redwood/shot/286112

Maya: hypothesis: when prefetch + fp8 quantization combo hits particular QK distribution the softmax under/overflow cascades. prefetch can produce slightly misaligned KV pointers if interleaving of batching changes. try disabling kv_prefetch to reproduce.

Ava: ran quick repro with kv_prefetch=false and same kernel flag: no NaNs in 10k samples. command: 
```bash
./run_infer --kernel flashx-quant --quant fp8 --kv-prefetch false --batch 32 --seq 153 --dataset eval-longhist
```
results: output_nan_ratio=0.0 p99 back to baseline.

Sam: OK that points at interaction. two-pronged plan: (1) fast mitigation — add numeric guardrail in kernel selector to choose stable fp16/bf16 kernel when extreme qk values detected; (2) longer-term — investigate prefetch pointer arithmetic in paged path.

Maya: agreed. for (1) propose a cheap pre-check using per-request scan of qk_max and qk_std. If qk_max - qk_mean > T (empirically 1e3 for our models) then force "stable" kernel. Pseudocode: 
```py
def choose_kernel(qk_stats, batch_meta):
    if qk_stats.max - qk_stats.mean > T or batch_meta.seq_len > 120:
        return 'fp16-stable-fused'
    return 'flashx-quant'
```

Rajat: microbench: switching to stable path reduces tokens/sec by ~9% but eliminates NaNs. Also add a hysteresis counter (don't flip for single request) to avoid oscillation. For batching heuristics: prefer fused variant when avg_seq_len > 80 and batch_size < 48; keep flashx for short sequences.

Ava: what's the rollout plan? canary per-route? we need automated rollback if NaN rate > 0.5%/minute.

Sam: I'll land a patch to kernel_selector: add numeric_score = qk_max - qk_mean and a prefetched_kv_flag. If numeric_score > THRESH or prefetched_kv_flag true and seq_len>120 -> pick stable kernel. Add unit tests + canary gate in deploy. Patch PR: https://repo.redwood/infra/pull/7042

Maya: also add a small softmax clamp before exponentiation as defensive programming in quant kernels: clamp_logits = clip(logits, -L, L) with L derived per-model (maybe 30-40). reduces extreme exps.

Sam: good. I'll add that as runtime-config toggled flag so we can experiment without rebuilding kernels.

perf-bot: alerting updated: NaN-rate > 0.2% triggers paging rollback to previous kernel; canary metrics added for per-route nan_rate, p99, tokens/s. :white_check_mark:

Ava: thanks. I'll follow up with a short postmortem and repro script for eng-runtime.

Rajat: one more note — add a nightly micro-benchmark sweep that runs combos: {kernel variants} x {kv_prefetch on/off} x {seq lengths}. captured regression pattern in JSON under /benchshots/286112-guardrail.json.

Sam: schedule: patch today, canary tomorrow, rollback strategy in place.

Ava: :rocket:
